A lot of potential, but since there's so little content it feels like the only way they could introduce longevity was to make it waaaay too grindy. I'm just not interested in doing another 40min run so I can increase my critical hit chance by 1% Ship feels too sluggish, especially when your job is to fly directly at projectiles so that you can shoot the things firing them. No dodging in and out here! The implementation of an infinitely tall corridor doesn't really hold up when you approach the "ceiling" and a wireframe appears to restrict you. Which is fine, but by the time it shows up and you've been made aware that you're at the ceiling, and no you can't go up the extra foot to clear the wall, then you get to crash into the wall.. Enemies are...whatever. Giving them all the same colour palette might not be the best approach to make them interesting. Anyway. You might get a couple of hours out if.

I want to like it, but there are a few issues, such as pacing. The one that bothers me the most is that in Starfox, pressing the shoulder buttons flipped your ship on its side, while double-tapping performed a barrel roll. In this game, you CAN'T flip your ship on its side—only barrel roll. Something about that just breaks the feeling of control over your ship. I feel like I'm flying a brick, not a starship.

I absolutely LOVED this idea. Starfox Roguelight? Cool aesthetic! Music. The works. Then they took the tilt funtion out. I had no idea this would be the fulcrum my enjoyment of this game rests on, but here we are. So remember in Starfox you hit L or R and you tip left or right, and then double tapping that button does the famous barrel roll. It gave you a little zippy fighter pilot control. You used it to slip through cracks. Timed those barrel rolls to deflect projectiles. That was here. WAS here. They turned it into this single button (tutorial still says doubletap. it is a lie) you cant tilts your ship. I hate it now. I hate how it feels. Its not fun to fly anymore and apparently that was it. I'm gona try to get a refund because but you know how it is with early access. I lost. Im disappointed at hell. I loved this until they broke it. The devs responded in steam forums, btw. To paraphrase, "We hear you and we still think this is better" so yeah. ♥♥♥♥ it. wish me luck, gang

I see a lot of reviews complaining about the lack of tilt controls. I have not played the game before the 1.0 release so I guess I'm lucky there I don't have the disappointment of missing those controls. This game is vaguely similar to Backpack Hero. There's passive story telling between levels, the gameplay is fairly simple with increasingly difficult enemy types as the run progresses. Each level you get 3 choices between upgrades, and you can build up damage, dodge, speed, and other types of builds. There's in-game modifications (difficulty modifiers) that give you more game currency to unlock stuff faster and a separate section for challenges. I've had a lot of fun in this game. Something you can play a video in the background and listen to while you play this. I wish there was more story though. The game is very stable and runs well. I've had no crashes, nor framerate drops. I'm running a Windows 10, RTX 2060, i7-9700 at 1080p.

Conflicted. I do like this game, with a lot of caveats though. -Love the soundtrack -Love the voice acting (mostly. Especially Sandy Can.) -Love the artstyle. Simplistic but stylistic. -Controls wonderfully. That said, I'm not still not sure I'd recommend it. -Three Levels. Three and a half technically. It gets old very quickly. After you've reached the end just once, you've experienced 95% of the game. As a game with rougelike elements, you're supposed to play over and over, but I'm struggling, man. Three levels with the same enemies, and very little variance between runs, because there really aren't very many powerups either, and the ones that exist don't drastically change how you play. There aren't very many bosses, so yet again, there's a serious lack of variance there. I really wish there'd be more like flying challenges or something, because as it stands, the only thing you can really is boost through tight holes every now and then. Also the story is very awkwardly told. They're trying to do the Hades thing where you get a bit more story after every run, but the cut-offs are random as hell. Conversations just stop sometimes and it's really weird.. I can feel the budget limitations, which is sad for a game where everything else is actually really good. I wish there was a 'middle thumb' option on Steam, because I'd recommend this...on sale.

I can see and appreciate the effort, but the result is not good. What we have here is a short on content, incoherent mix of a runner, an on-rails shooter and an action roguelike, built on repurposed tech to a substandard quality. You could see in the trailer everything nice about Whisker Squadron, so I'm going to be fully disagreeable here. First, the obvious. This is not a survivors game, in any way, at all. Putting "Survivor" in a title was a ♥♥♥♥ move: they don't have the necessary vibes (I mean, it's a frantic shooter), and what they actually borrowed doesn't cohere with the rest at all: gem collecting conflicts with the main gameplay, and missable gems aren't exactly appealing. Meanwhile, it doesn't even seem to be a good marketing, given how crowded is the survivors market now. The action part here is on the fence between a runner and a shooter, unable to pick a side, resulting in suffering. On a runner side, we have cluttered maps you're supposed to maneuver through, and a "tight boost" mechanic encouraging you to rush through narrow openings. On a shooter side, we have enemies shooting you at angles, and a combo mechanic encouraging you to kill enemies regularly. Nobody forbids enemies from disappearing from you for the combo cooldown duration - yes, combo has a cooldown. Nobody forbids enemies from shooting you from around the corner. Have fun. Meanwhile, enemy variety is meh, weapons variety is also meh, and weapon limits - one primary weapon, one secondary that requires pickups for ammo refill - are kind of insane. Tying together moving and aiming (one stick/mouse to rule them all) is... a design choice, I guess. Boss phase changes and stage selection break the remains of the flow. Graphic design here is hostile to the player: you often stop detecting enemies/projectiles in your own weapon fire VFX. Also, color coding - blue vs. lilac, really? - is weak enough to require full color sight to tell apart enemy fire from pickups (say, XP vs. lasers) even in normal situations. Also, it's hard to judge distances here (both for collisions, pickups and weapon effects) On the roguelike part, you have all the standard trappings: XP/levels/upgrade choices, extremely watered down Slay The Spire-style map, all wrapped into the standard unlock-/numerical metaprogression. Upgrades are, for the most part, tied either to "tight boost" or combo; a half of them either outright useless or situational, most others are boring, hilarious cheese is non-existent. Map is also boring, the stage variety boils down to what powerup stages you pick, and how many "hard" battles you fight (hards are hit-or-miss, powerups tend to be either underwhelming or strictly necessary). Metaprogression is, again, boring: the unlocks don't change gameplay too much, numerical bonuses don't either - there is nothing transformative like +projectile count or +perk level. There is simply not much content here. The balance is off in extremely unfun way: for example, one type of powerup stage gives a random bonus of +50% to primary weapon damage, with one alternative being a bunch of metacurrency. Seriously? Meanwhile, there are persistent and annoying bugs, such as parts of your build randomly disappearing or simply stopping working. Also, 100% grind is obnoxious.

Roguelites can be hit or miss for me. I'm not opposed to them but it's not a style I'm inherently drawn to either. But Whisker Squadron: Survivor got its hooks in instantly and never let go. Near six hours and a fully completed run later I can safely say I adore this game. To start with the most important part, this is an excellent Star Fox style shooter. Tight controls, punchy weapons with a great enemy roster to use them on, and a super charming cartoon cyber-neon aesthetic with a killer soundtrack. It's the perfect foundation for the progression systems to build on, hitting that "just one more run" sweet spot. Each of the three acts features a randomized branching layout, letting you prioritize stages with bonus conditions or opportunities to collect additional powerups. There's a wide array of upgrades you can collect during runs and some of them can open up some really fun new twists, like boosting through tight spaces to gain health or using your spin block to reflect projectiles back at enemies. Runs aren't radically unrecognizable from each other but there's good room for customization that gives each run personality. Like any game built on randomization sometimes you'll be at the mercy of the RNG more than others. But no run ever felt truly unwinnable. Between runs you can also unlock more permanent boosts to basic stats as well as new weapons, ships, and pilots at specific milestones. Progression comes at a fairly steady pace. I can see some folks potentially burning out on the game quickly if they're the type to really grind for unlocks. You won't be buying everything in a hurry. But if you focus on playing for fun and letting things open up as you go, you'll find a healthy selection of new toys waiting for you each time you feel tempted to try another run. Playing for fun really is the key here because the game is a joy. This is one of my new arcade favorites, and I can see myself picking this up for a run here or there for a long time to come. I'll be first in line when its currently unnamed sequel takes off.

I'd only reccommend this game if you find it on sale as it feels like only just a extra-mode in a Starfox-like game rather than a full game. The reason I say that is due to how repetitive the enemies and levels are, which makes sense for a rogue-lite but is counter to what makes a game like Starfox good. Starfox 64 is known as a timeless classic because of the tight level design, voiced character dialogue, and branching paths all leading to a memorable experience. In this game you will be flying solo down trench the whole time. Whisker Squadron: Survivor is still pretty fun once you get a decent build going, but it takes a while to get there as your first 5 or so runs will put tutorials for mechanics at the start of each one. The result is that when you first start the game it feels very barebones as most of the fun features to play aren't available until you fail a few runs.

I feel like I'm given the bare minimum of weapon upgrades per "level". I'm never allowed to be OP because the enemies scale to your damage.

Do not buy. The developer has admitted on LinkedIn that the studio is essentially shut down and the team has been let go due to funding issues. They slapped a "1.0" label on this game to call it "finished," but it’s an unfinished product used to squeeze the last bit of cash out of backers and fans. The main open-world game that this was supposed to fund is now a ghost ship. Total lack of transparency and a betrayal of the community's trust.

Sure the game is fun when you get a bunch of upgrades and you're mowing down scores of enemies none stop, but by the time I got to that point the game just slowed enemy spawns to a crawl and I only had like two levels left and I really didn't want to start over. Also the story seems like a first draft based on improv. "Surpise! You are in a space ship being interviewed for a job! Start from there" just not that intersting I would recommend giving this one a skip. There's nothing you can't get from other better games

This was supposed to be the prequel to a fully fledged shooter game in the vein of Star Fox. Unfortunately, the developer insisted on making a lot of changes that were mostly disliked by the community, and the game kept limping along until... the studio closed down and they didn't mention this anywhere but a LinkedIn post that most users would never see. The CEO is now working on a new project, while everyone who helped fund this game and the development of the full version has been left in the dust. If there was ever an argument for not supporting early access... it's this game. A shame. Because it was fun and showed promise.

I really like it. It’s a compact yet entertaining arcade-style shooter. You can clear the three acts in about an hour, earning currency along the way to upgrade your ship or buy new vessels and weapons for another run through the game. If you find it too easy, you can make things a bit more difficult or interesting by enabling optional challenges. The visuals are clean and feature a stylish vaporwave aesthetic; the game runs smoothly and prioritizes functionality over cutting-edge graphics. I think the soundtrack is solid for an arcade game. And it has cats! I can highly recommend Whisker Squadron: Survivor.

I'm a fan! The style and vibes are fun, it looks and sounds great. I found it easy to jump into and replayable from the variety.
